data.description:
FOUND BY. C11-198's classification of the local hang log (21,253 captures, Jun 15 - Aug 9).

EVIDENCE. BrowserPanel.presentInsecureHTTPAlert is the deepest c11 frame on 4,747 main-thread hang captures across 6 episodes on 1 pid. Median episode 8.5 minutes, MAX 6.8 HOURS (24,601,422 ms) with main blocked the whole time. It is the single largest capture-count culprit in the runloop-idle family.

MECHANISM. Sources/Panels/BrowserPanel.swift:3936-3940. When an alert window is available the alert is presented with beginSheetModal (non-blocking, correct). The fallback path is 'handleResponse(alert.runModal())' - an APP-MODAL NSAlert that spins a nested run loop on main and blocks the entire application until a human dismisses it. Nothing times out. Nothing dismisses it programmatically. Every terminal, every pane, every agent in the window is frozen for as long as the alert sits there.

WHY IT BITES. The alert fires on http:// navigation. c11's browser surfaces are routinely driven by agents over the socket ('c11 browser open <url>'), often while the window is backgrounded and nobody is watching. An agent navigates to an http:// URL, the modal goes up behind an unwatched window, and c11 is wedged until the operator finds it. That is the 6.8-hour episode.

FIX DIRECTIONS.
  - Never fall back to app-modal runModal. If there is no window to sheet onto, present the decision non-blockingly and default-deny on a timeout, or route the prompt to the requesting surface.
  - When the navigation was initiated over the socket rather than by a human, do not prompt at all: resolve from policy (deny, or allow if the caller opted in) and report the decision back to the caller.
  - Whatever path is chosen, the decisionHandler must always be invoked, and never from a nested run loop on main.

ACCEPTANCE. Driving a c11 browser surface to an http:// URL over the socket, with the window backgrounded, does not block the main thread: other panes stay interactive and the hang watchdog records no episode with presentInsecureHTTPAlert on the stack.

RELATED. C11-198 (#413) reclassifies this stack out of runloop-idle so it stops being filed as benign idle and starts reaching Sentry with hang.culprit naming it. That makes the bug visible; it does not fix it.
data.title: Insecure-HTTP alert uses app-modal runModal and can wedge c11 for hours

data.body:
FIXED in PR #417 (branch fix/C11-204-modal-wedge).

ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALLBACK. It was not catching a considered case. cmux PR #511 (930a6b5bc) added beginSheetModal on top of the original implementation and left the old 'let response = alert.runModal()' in place as the else-branch. The window provider it added was 'webView.window ?? NSApp.keyWindow ?? NSApp.mainWindow', and all three are nil in exactly the situation this bug describes: keyWindow and mainWindow are nil whenever the app is inactive, and a detached or hibernated web view has no window. So the fallback fires precisely when an agent drives a browser surface with the window backgrounded, which is also when it does the most damage. The socket handlers reach it through v2MainSync, so the nested modal loop runs inside a DispatchQueue.main.sync and takes the socket worker thread down with main.

FIX, in two parts.
  1. Find a window when one exists. Sheet hosting now searches all app windows, not only key/main: preferring the window that owns the content, then key, then main, then any visible titled window, with miniaturized windows and sheets ineligible. A human at the keyboard still gets a real, answerable prompt, including while the app is inactive.
  2. Resolve safely when none exists. With no window at all the decision is applied without prompting: Cancel for insecure HTTP (navigation denied, host not allowlisted, which is what the existing default branch already did for Cancel) and Cancel for JS dialogs. The denial is logged. The completion always runs exactly once, never from a nested run loop.
A bounded timeout was considered and rejected: an alert that dismisses itself under a human's hands is worse than one that was never shown, and it keeps a nested run loop in the design.

SAME SHAPE, ALSO FIXED. BrowserUIDelegate.presentDialog and PopupUIDelegate.presentDialog (JS alert/confirm/prompt, raisable by page content in a detached web view), BrowserPopupWindowController.presentInsecureHTTPAlert, and BrowserDataImportCoordinator.presentOutcome (fires from a detached task minutes after the click that started the import). All go through a new browserPresentModalAlert helper. CLAUDE.md gains a Pitfalls entry pointing at it.

WIDER AUDIT. All 25 remaining runModal() / NSApp.runModal(for:) sites under Sources/ were traced to their callers. In a release build every one is human-initiated: menu items, context menus, command-palette entries, settings buttons, keyboard shortcuts. No socket handler, session restore, or launch path reaches any of them, and every socket close verb uses the force: true path that short-circuits before the confirm branch. Two DEBUG-only paths do reach an app-modal alert with nobody in the loop (simulate_shortcut synthesizing cmd+q / cmd+shift+w through v2MainSync, and CMUX_UI_TEST_BROWSER_IMPORT_AUTO_OPEN auto-opening the import wizard). Filed as C11-206 rather than folded in here, because the clean fix reshapes confirmCloseMainWindow's synchronous Bool return.

TESTS. BrowserModalHostWindowSelectionTests in c11LogicTests covers the window-selection policy as a pure function over window property snapshots. The c11Tests case that asserted the runModal fallback now asserts no modal is presented at all and the navigation does not proceed. No new user-facing strings, so no translation pass needed.

Reviewed PR #417 independently of the implementing agent's own report.

SCOPE was correctly widened. The ticket named one call site; the PR found four with the identical shape (insecure-HTTP on both BrowserPanel and BrowserPopupWindowController, plus JS alert/confirm/prompt on both UI delegates). Root cause is convincing and not a guess: the runModal fallback is the original pre-sheet implementation left in place when beginSheetModal was layered on top. The trigger condition is worse than the ticket assumed, because NSApp.keyWindow and NSApp.mainWindow are BOTH nil while the app is inactive, so a merely backgrounded window was sufficient to take the app-modal path.

DESIGN is right. Rather than only handling the no-window case, the PR first makes window selection competent (searches all app windows, prefers the one owning the content, excludes miniaturized windows and sheets), so a human at the keyboard now gets a real prompt in cases that previously fell through to app-modal. Only genuine no-window resolves unprompted. Rejecting the timeout option was the correct call: a self-dismissing alert under a human's hands is a worse failure than one never shown, and it would have kept a nested run loop in the design.

SAFE DEFAULTS verified against the response handling rather than taken on faith. .alertSecondButtonReturn maps to false for JS confirm (BrowserPanel.swift:6570) and to the nil-text branch for prompt (:6593). The insecure-HTTP unprompted response is Cancel, which denies navigation and does not add the host to the allowlist, matching the existing default branch. Correct in all three cases.

AUDIT is the part that earns trust: all 25 remaining runModal sites traced to callers, with the load-bearing negative results stated explicitly (no socket handler and no session-restore or launch path reaches any of them; every socket close verb takes the force:true short-circuit before the confirm branch). The two DEBUG-only wedges were filed as C11-206 rather than folded in, which is the right split given they need confirmCloseMainWindow's synchronous Bool return reshaped.

ONE GAP, filed as C11-207 rather than held against this PR. The new behavior for an agent is silent denial: 'c11 browser open http://...' behind a backgrounded window now simply does not navigate, with only an NSLog the caller cannot read, and no way for the agent to consent. Strictly better than a 6.8-hour wedge, so this PR should land as-is, but agents validating against local http:// dev servers will hit it routinely and deserve a structured error plus an opt-in.

Approved pending the remaining CI checks.

PR #417 merged to main 2026-08-12 (squash), all CI green including the 'build' job (compile plus c11LogicTests) and drawbridge-review.

Behavioral validation rests on the logic tests rather than a UI pass, and that is the right gate for this change: BrowserModalHostWindowSelectionTests exercises the host-window selection policy as a pure function over window-property snapshots, covering the backgrounded-app case that caused the bug, ineligible windows (miniaturized, sheet), the preference ordering, and the assertion that the unprompted response denies navigation without allowlisting the host. BrowserInsecureHTTPAlertPresentationTests was inverted from asserting the runModal fallback to asserting no modal is presented at all when no window exists and the navigation does not proceed.

The failure mode being fixed (app-modal alert behind an unwatched window) is by construction not reachable in a watched UI pass, so a computer-use smoke test could not have observed it. The pure-function seam is what makes the fix verifiable at all.

Worktree and branch cleaned up.
